verdict.summary: GitHub documents direct OAuth app registration and user authorization, but the claims do not explicitly state whether GitHub performs a provider review before use. Organization owners may separately need to approve the app, and users must approve newly added repository or organization permissions.

calendar.label: No official registration or review wait is stated

variants.summary: Register an OAuth app under a personal account or an organization where you have administrative access, and request the needed read scopes.
Register an OAuth app and request the required write scopes; organization restrictions may require owner approval.
Outside users can authorize the OAuth app, but organizations using access restrictions may require approval before non-public resources are accessible.
Request write scopes and account for user approval of newly added repository or organization permissions and possible organization-owner approval.

byo_advice: Composio's managed GitHub app is sufficient when its authentication, scopes, and connection behavior meet your needs; use your own OAuth app when you need separate credentials, controlled scopes, or organization-specific access. In GitHub Settings, open Developer settings, select OAuth apps, and click New OAuth App or Register a new application. Enter the app name, full website URL, optional description, and Composio's authorization callback URL; then copy the generated client ID and client secret into the Composio auth config. Request read or write scopes as needed, enable Device Flow only in a constrained environment, and abort authorization when the returned state does not match the supplied state.

steps.title: Sign in to GitHub
steps.detail: Sign in to the developer’s GitHub account and open the profile menu. The new-app URL is https://github.com/settings/applications/new, but it redirects to sign-in when unauthenticated.

evidence.label: UNCERTAIN
evidence.note: Check the developer’s account sign-in and whether personal-account or organization ownership is intended.

steps.title: Open the OAuth app registration page
steps.detail: Open Settings, select Developer settings, then OAuth apps. Click New OAuth App; for a first app, the button is labeled Register a new application.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: In the upper-right corner of any page on GitHub, click your profile picture, then click Settings.

steps.title: Register your own OAuth app
steps.detail: Open the registration form and prepare a public application name, full website URL, optional description, and authorization callback URL. Only use information suitable for public display and avoid internal URLs.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: Only use information in your OAuth app that you consider public. Avoid using sensitive data, such as internal URLs, when creating an OAuth app.

steps.title: Set the Composio callback URL
steps.detail: Enter Composio’s callback as the app’s authorization callback URL. Do not add a wildcard unless it is specifically required and the associated risk has been assessed.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: Enabling wildcard matching can expose your app to security risks

steps.title: Submit the registration
steps.detail: Submit the OAuth app registration and wait for GitHub to create the application. This registration must represent the developer’s own app rather than relying on a managed-app configuration.

evidence.label: UNCERTAIN
evidence.note: Check the exact registration button and whether GitHub displays any provider-level review requirement for this OAuth app.

steps.title: Connect the credentials to Composio
steps.detail: Retrieve the app’s client ID and client secret, then paste them into the GitHub custom OAuth auth configuration in Composio. Keep the secret confidential and test the connection with the intended account.

evidence.label: UNCERTAIN
evidence.note: Check Composio’s current BYO GitHub auth-config field names and test procedure.

steps.title: Obtain customer and organization approval
steps.detail: Ask each customer organization to approve the app when its OAuth access restrictions require it. Approval can be necessary before the app can access that organization’s non-public resources.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: For organizations with OAuth app access restrictions, you can request that organization owners approve the application for use in that organization.

evidence.label: DOCS

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: The access token expires after eight hours, and the refresh token expires after six months without use.

gotchas.text: Creating more than ten tokens for the same user and scope combination causes GitHub to revoke an existing token with that combination.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: If an application creates more than ten tokens for the same user and the same scopes, GitHub revokes one of the existing tokens with the same user/application/scope combination

blockers.symptom: The callback is rejected or authorization does not return to Composio.
blockers.cause: The registered callback URL differs from Composio’s required callback URL.
blockers.fix: Set the authorization callback URL to https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback and retest.

evidence.label: UNCERTAIN
evidence.note: Verify the exact callback field and whether the same value must also be configured in Composio.

blockers.symptom: The app cannot access a customer organization’s non-public resources.
blockers.cause: The organization has OAuth access restrictions and has not approved the app.
blockers.fix: Request approval from the organization owner, then have the user authorize it again.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: If the organization does not approve the application, then the application will only be able to access the organization's public resources.

blockers.symptom: An existing user token disappears after additional token creation.
blockers.cause: The same user/application/scope combination exceeded the ten-token limit.
blockers.fix: Avoid unnecessary token creation and have affected users re-authorize as needed.

evidence.label: DOCS
evidence.quote: There is a limit of ten tokens that are issued per user/application/scope combination

scopes.why: Use only if refresh-capable user authorization is needed; it provides an expiring access token and refresh token.
